author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A Fall River man has been sentenced to time served after admitting that he mailed cocaine from California to Massachusetts, federal prosecutors said Thursday.

Justin Dupras, 44, received a sentence of two days already served in U.S. District Court in Boston. He pleaded guilty in May 2025 to attempted possession of cocaine with intent to distribute. The sentence resolves the federal criminal charge described in the government’s case.

Prosecutors said Dupras mailed approximately two kilograms of cocaine from Los Angeles to Fall River on December 17, 2024, returned to Massachusetts and collected the package two days later. Investigators also linked him to earlier shipments of more than two kilograms from Chino Hills in September 2024 and about two kilograms from Los Angeles the following month.

Flight records showed same-day return trips connected to the shipments, according to prosecutors. The U.S. Postal Inspection Service investigated with Fall River police. The announced sentence concerns Dupras’s attempt to receive the December package and does not alter the government’s description of the earlier suspected shipments.
dek: Federal prosecutors said the defendant shipped kilogram quantities from California before collecting a package in Fall River.
headline: Fall River man sentenced in California cocaine-mailing case
